issues.description: Predicate `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` buries the intent; extract a named helper.
issues.detail: The contract is: a block-less `@layer` statement is allowed before `@import`, but a block-bearing `@layer` rule is not. The negated condition forces readers to simulate De Morgan. Extract `isLayerStatement(node)` (or similar) so the call site states the invariant positively and survives future maintenance.

issues.description: `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` leaks PostCSS internals; use the AST contract directly.
issues.detail: Distinguishing block-less at-rules by probing for `undefined` couples correctness to a PostCSS implementation detail rather than the documented Container-vs-leaf distinction. Prefer `node.nodes == null` (codebase convention) or a typed `isAtRule(node) && !('nodes' in node)` check so the abstraction boundary holds across AST refinements.

issues.description: Tests assert the new reject case but not the symmetric accept case for `@layer foo;` before `@import`.
issues.detail: The diff adds one positive failure case (`@layer foo {}` before `@import`) but no test pins the still-allowed statement form (`@layer foo;` before `@import` must not report). Without this complementary case, a future refactor could tighten the predicate and silently regress substitutability of the statement form.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously agrees the fix is behaviorally correct: it restores the CSS spec distinction between `@layer` statements (block-less, allowed before `@import`) and `@layer` rules (with block, not allowed). All three reviewers flag the same two stylistic concerns and the same test-coverage gap. The predicate is written by negation-of-absence and leaks PostCSS internals via `typeof ... === 'undefined'`; extracting a named helper and using the AST contract directly would make the invariant self-evident. Tests pin the bug but not the symmetric accept case, leaving the boundary unverified. Merge-worthy after these P2 cleanups.
